lore.en:
Radames was the Monastery's confessor, who had dedicated his life to hear the vile sins the monks had committed. Generation after generation, he quietly listened to words of guilt and repentance from everyone who came searching for forgiveness. His ears, brimmed with sins that his infallible memory could never erase.

His body grew old, nourished only by an immense guilt, so vast it would not let him die. He stopped feeling hunger, thirst, pleasure or even pain. Only the burden existed, the burden of every wrong now etched into his soul. Thus, he had become a tool, a prisoner of the sacrament of confession.

Some monks claimed the souls of their fallen brothers sought the aid of Radames, even after death. Hoping his absolution could bridge the abyss separating them from eternal rest.

The confessor accumulated such a heavy burden. His weakened body could no longer contain the depth of his corrupted knowledge. From his agonised flesh sprouted a thousand voices, speaking words of sin, like dreaded whispers spreading through the chambers of the monastery in spectral echoes, looking for a way out.

Those horrifying sounds flowed over the walls and statues, eroding the very stone with their sinister vibrations, smothering everything in a choking grey dust. It was as if the sins themselves wanted to be buried. Thus, the monastery fell silent.

lore.en:
Sheltered by the shadows that reigned within the ceilings of that abandoned palace, Orospina laughed. Her silhouette insinuated in the dim light, aristocratic clothing made of burgundy and white silk crowned by a delicate mask of ornate porcelain.

From the panelling up high hung thin strands of pure gold, a trapeze for her aerial dance that she used to attack with the precision of a wasp. Far below, the corpses of intruders fool enough to enter her domain piled up against the luxurious marble, crimson now with their blood.

Yet one victim clung to life. His eyes ever darting from shadow to shadow, in a fruitless search for his executioner. On the edge of his vision, the sheen of her sword appeared and vanished: a long, thin rapier that reflected the shine of the candlelight and gold decorating the grim halls. Orospina, delighted by the agony and fear of her prey, patiently waited for the perfect moment to deliver her deadly strike. A thrust, a muted scream, then silence. The palace, once more velveted by riches and death.

lore.en:
The axe fell with a sharp thud. The head of Lesmes the martyr, severed from its neck, rolled down the steps, spilling blood on the cold stone. The inquisitors, unperturbed and proud in their garnished thrones, stared sternly at the result of their relentless prosecution.

With every eye focused on ensuring judgment was passed, nobody noticed a small girl, her head covered by a hood, sneaking past the iron grating to steal the martyr’s head.

She ran away before anyone noticed her, as invisible on the way out as she had been on entering. The girl took the head in her tiny hands and carried it to a long-abandoned church. Once in, she found her way to the gloomy sacristy in the back, where a dusty urn of glass was kept. With great care she opened it, removing the velvet cushion inside that held an assortment of small bones. Without any regard for the relics, she threw them aside, replacing them with the martyr’s head. The girl stared long and gravely at her work before curling up on the ground next to it and fell asleep.

lore.en:
The executioners waited until the ravenous flames devoured the condemned before approaching the stake to collect their charred remains. Amidst the cindered wood and ashes, they found the body of a woman, untouched by the fire. Her skin, while cold and pale as marble, looked pure, unblemished. 

Awestruck were the executioners by this finding and long they wondered who this saint was, as it was clear that the divine will of the Miracle had protected her flesh from the pyre. They would never know, but her body, still preserved and immaculate, rests within the most delicate of urns. This beautiful work of glass and silver, placed in the bowels of a crypt, under a church erected in her honour.

“Shed no more tears my brother. While I must go, my being will always watch over you. No matter how vast the abyss is that separate us, my voice will always find a way to echo within your heart.” said Perpetva to her brother Esdras.

As he cradled her head within his trembling arms, her eyes closed for a final time, thus Esdras heeded her words and cried no more.

Its surface shimmered, glowing oddly in the dim light of the few candles found in that somber chamber.

One day, during his habitual walk, he wandered deep into the forest to pray, coming back a changed man. As if his mind had returned to a more joyous, more hopeful era.” said the woman to the stranger, as her gaze lingered, sympathetically, over the friar.

The old man gestured endlessly to the air, a smile uplifting his withered face.

lore.en:
One night, the young Regula, and we will never know if she did this out of curiosity or boredom, crept into the workshop of the famous sculptress of her village.

She wanted to be the first to behold her newest piece, the one so eagerly waited for by everyone: the effigy of the Saint. She froze, just as she entered, struck with awe in the presence of such beautiful work, which paint had still to dry. Regula then felt a perverse urge, and taking a cloth, pressed down against the face of the Saint, stealing all colour from the sculpture visage.

She then covered her own face with the fabric, pretending that the Saint’s beauty was now hers. The young woman played with her painted cloth, mimicking the pious gesture of the Saint, dreaming of the villagers' devotion.

After which, it was time to leave, lest the sculptress discovered her mischief. But upon removing the cloth she discovered, horrified, that the reflection on one of the windows showed no features of her face. In its place remained a shapeless stump of ashen flesh, dry and cracked like charred wood. Regula’s scream pierced the night, as she understood the punishment for her sin.

lore.en:
The baby cried, screaming and thrashing in the arms of his father. Cesareo, full of sadness and sorrow, sought in vain to calm his child, cradling him on his thick arms.
 
“He hungers…” Cesareo repeated to himself, his voice stained with guilt. The body of his wife lay besides him, as a terrible sickness had recently claimed her, brought on, or so Cesareo believed, by some unfair and relentless divine punishment.

Looking at his son, seeing how small and famished he was, Cesareo entrusted himself to the will of the Miracle, praying for a breast full with milk so he could save the baby’s life. In desperation, he let grief guide his confused hands in an act of pained madness. He took a knife to his wife’s corpse, severing a breast. Then, with thread and needle, stitched it to his own chest.

“Is this what you demand of me? Is this what it takes for you to listen to my plea?” howled Cesareo. And so it happened that, from the amputated breast, dropped a single tear of a pale, creamy, gleaming liquid. The man, bewildered, held his child and the baby suckled. Cesareo moved to wipe away his tears, and in that moment realised that his son now lay still. For he had turned into a statue of wax.

lore.en:
He had finally found it! The young monk had spent years searching for that book among the mountain of relics in the abby's great library. A book that he believed to be one of the great, lost forbidden works. Unable to control his impatience, he hid it under his robe and crept toward his dorm, eager to unravel its secrets under the cover of night. With the room plunged into shadows and only the flickering light of a candle as a witness, he began to read. The words came to life, dancing before his eyes, conjuring images of heresies that flooded his mind. At the same time, something far more ominous was happening: as he advanced, his conscious thoughts vanished, erased by a hidden force, as if the price of his audacity was oblivion.

Desperate to preserve the forbidden knowledge, the monk attempted to transcribe the passages, but the letters revolted against him in his pen, twisting into indecipherable hieroglyphs. Frustration consumed him, his sanity hung by a thread. Overcome by exhaustion, he succumbed to slumber at his desk. By dawn, the book was gone, and with it, any memory of the previous night. Not even the memory of having possessed the enigmatic volume remained. All traces of its existence had vanished, as if it had never been more than a fleeting dream.

lore.en:
In the gloom of the cathedral, a beggar on his knees extended his trembling hands outward toward the passing bishop. His eyes, cloudy with despair, fixated upon the imposing figure who overshadowed the beggar with its presence. “Have mercy on me, please, your excellency!” he begged with a broken voice, clinging to the edges of the purple cassock that caressed the cold marble.
The bishop, whose stern countenance betrayed no shadow of compassion, looked with disdain upon the man who had dared to sully his sacred vestment. “Get your hands off me, pauper,” he snapped coldly, his voice echoing through the Gothic arches. He forcefully removed the hands that were clinging to him and continued on his way, leaving behind an echo of hurtful words and the torn soul of the beggar in the shadow of the great temple.

The townsfolk greet her, but she does not respond to them. Her gaze remains fixed on the ground, and her lips utter nothing but prayers. She dresses in strictly black, as if she were in mourning for something greater than life itself.

lore.en: “Kneeling, I held the knife, pointing it toward my chest. I reflected on how I had ended up in such a desperate situation, on the verge of committing the most terrible act imaginable. The image of myself made me react. What was I doing? I tried to drop the knife immediately, but something stopped me! My hands gripped the blade tightly against my will. Terrified, I tried with all my might to push away the knife from my heart. My body was shaking violently. Suddenly, I was able to rid myself of the invisible force that was controlling me. Freedom brought instant remorse, a pang of regret for having overstepped boundaries in my great distress. The Miracle had been merciful.”

lore.en: In a forgotten corner of the cemetery, the mother and her daughters performed their mysterious ritual. Each month, without fail, they placed a wreath on a strange, unmarked grave. No one knew who lay there, but the three seemed to share a deep bond with the deceased. They prayed together, their voices whispering secrets to the night wind. By dawn, the flowers had withered, as if absorbing the sadness that enveloped the family. The locals would gossip about the power of their mourning, while the women simply continued their solemn vigil.

lore.en:
The inquisitor, his gaze unrelented, pronounced the words that would seal the prisoner’s fate: “You will remain here, chained beneath the blade, until one of the crowd assembled dares to be your executioner. Your life hangs by an invisible thread, sustained by the public’s indecision. They will decide when you will take your last breath.” And yet no one dared to step forward. Some, plagued by fear and doubt, tried approaching the chopping block. However, fear paralyzed them and they inevitably retreated, unable to carry out the sentence.

Far from a mercy, the wait became agonizing to the condemned. The prisoner, with wild eyes, cried out to those around him. His desperate screams echoed in the air, but the crowd remained motionless. In desperation, the prisoner insulted them, provoked them, damned them... But his words fell on deaf ears.

The inquisitors departed. The crowd also dispersed, as if the tragedy had lost its hold on them. Only the prisoner was left there, chained. The Miracle, in an act of cruel benevolence, had touched him. He no longer felt thirst or hunger, just a gnawing desperation eating away at his soul.

Time passed mercilessly. The prisoner, in his isolation, soon forgot how he had earned his sentence. He simply longed for the end of his nightmare. That someone, out of compassion or cruelty, would dare to free him from his existence, suspended between life and death.

lore.en:
As he did every night, upon the priest retreating to his quarters and the church filling only with silence, the young sexton Hieron ignited the old bronze thurible. A family heirloom, he had received it from his father as he, before him, had inherited it from his own. As sacred fumes of the incense permeated the wood, he felt honoured by the task.

That night, upon commencing the ancient rite, the smoke grew thick and heavy, quickly expanding until the room choked from its cloying presence.

Hieron coughed and stumbled, dizzy after breathing the fumes, finally fainting before the statue of the Saint. That night the wind was fierce and through an open window a dust devil of dry leaves entered, swirling across the floor, hungry for the embers of the thurible.

Hieron woke to witness the statue aflame before his eyes. It was too late. He raised his gaze to the Saint’s face and, seized by the horror of the event and the guilt he felt, the sexton could swear the statue’s stare had twisted into one of reproach.

And so did the young man run, away from that church, horror chiselled in his childish face. He would never forget that hieratic figure with its stern, incriminating gaze, that had been his charge and duty during his whole life.

The act was witnessed, the criminal caught.
No trial needed, just a lesson to be taught.
Then an angry man, with fury in his eyes,
claimed to be the owner of the stolen prize.

With a threatening voice and eyes red with grief
he swore to cut the hands off the poor thief
He pulled out his blade and readied a hack
for he knew there'd be mercy if he did not act.

The soldiers stood aside, they just looked on
as the man commenced to bloodily right the wrong
The thief's fortune changed credit to that knife
He received his lesson but he kept his life

Though this act seemed merciless on its face
Unintended mercy comes from that strange place
The death-marked thief continued to be
thanks to the enraged man, who changed his destiny.

lore.en:
In the hidden gardens of the old monastery, a novice immersed himself in a silent ritual. At the usual time, he retired to a leafy, wooded area. There, among the rustling of the leaves and the aroma of wet earth, he shed a river of tears that seemed to flood out from the depths of his soul.

The other monks watched on in silence. They had come to recognize this familiar ritual of the hunched figure, face hidden in his hands. But the mystery that surrounded his cry remained unanswered. Some dared to ask him privately, but he would always respond with an evasive gesture, as if he were afraid of revealing a secret that did not belong to him. His eyes, however, betrayed a torment that weighed down on him.

And so the novice’s tears would filter through the corridors of the abbey, like a melancholic echo. The monks, accustomed to a life of ritual with prayers, chants, and daily tasks, accepted his pain as part of their routine. It was as if the young man were just another chime of the clock, a sad note in the symphony of their monastic lives.

lore.en:
In a vast desert, over which the sun hung relentlessly, a man walked. He was hesitant in his stride, each breath a whisper of life escaping. Thirst had consumed him to the point of desperation. With the last of his remaining strength slipping away, he leaned against a rock, and felt his body begin to falter.

It was then that a majestic eagle descended from the sky, landing on his chest with a grace that defied the cloud of death that surrounded the man. In his delirium, the man believed that the eagle was speaking to him with the solemnity of the heavens. “Close your eyes and give in to eternal rest. Your journey is over.” And so, in that immense sea of sand and solitude, the man closed his eyes, surrendering himself to the embrace of infinity, while the eagle took flight, leaving behind the serene silhouette of a liberated soul.

lore.en:
The priest’s young assistant found herself trapped in one of the dark repositories of the old church. The door closed behind her, and no one seemed to hear her desperate calls. The air became thick, and the darkness of the night seeped through the cracks in the wood, plunging the room into impenetrable blackness. The young woman clawed desperately at the walls of her unlikely prison, looking for something to help her find a way out. Her fingers came upon a forgotten candle in the corner. With a sigh of relief she managed to ignite it and its dim light revealed the contents of the repository.

Ancient figures of martyrs and saints, some of whose faces had been worn away by time, lined dusty shelves. But in the darkness, their outlines seemed to distort, assuming grotesque and threatening shapes. The faces of the martyrs twisted, transforming them into grimaces of suffering. The saints, whose pious glances had comforted generations, now seemed to look at her with hungry, malevolent eyes. Terror seized her and a scream escaped her lips.

Just then, the door burst open. The priest entered, holding a large lantern that illuminated the room. The figures returned to their original appearance: pious and holy.

lore.en:
We could see them. In the darkest corners of the ceilings. In the black found between the furniture. In every nook and cranny, we could see them shimmer. Those weird and gilded strands, that seemingly twisted around anything in sight, twinkling in the dim light of our trembling lamps with the same gleam of the jewels we hunted, the riches that lured us to these abandoned dwellings to begin with. After a long time spent exploring the vast alcoves, I found myself alone. Raising the lamp before me I frantically searched for my partners, finally spying their silhouettes far behind me.

Something was odd about the way they stayed, devoid of motion. I whispered their names and found no answer, thus retreated towards them.

My lamp revealing the same shimmer of those strange threads that infested this palace, only now entangled around the faces and bodies of my partners, restraining them in absolute silence. Turned into gilded statues by the same treasure we sought to steal, terror entwined on their inert faces.

I know not what they seek to find, of which treasure or mystery they would his corpse deprive. But here I stand before them, to protect him, to honour his memory and worth. And here I will stand until I my last breath, until my shield shatters and breaks, and only the splinters remain.2

Realising they were sealing me within, I cried out, but nobody answered. I have barely survived since then, sustained on breadcrumbs delivered through cracks in the door. Upon muddy water from an old clay pot. The convent has fallen into a sepulchral silence, broken occasionally by slow, heavy steps that can now be heard down the hallways. Something or someone has taken over this place. Please, to whomever finds this writing, please, have mercy and set me free from this nightmare.

lore.en:
That night the old painter was visited by the strangest and most disturbing of dreams. He saw himself as a guest at the table of two elders, siblings that engrossed themselves to the bitter vice of mutual disdain. Already sitting, they shot him uncomfortable smiles, and offered a meagre excuse for a dinner. The oldest, Castula, barraged her brother Trifon in constant slander, that he retorted back with disregard in an endless back and forth. Now and then they grinned at the painter, gestures loaded with hypocrisy that only made their cadaveric faces the more unsettling.

Shaken by the macabre surrounding that vision, the artist woke up in a flash of inspiration, and decided to capture that weird and anxious nightmare. The outlandish dream was then immortalised in a grim painting that invited the beholder to step inside the frame. Even if, by doing so, they risked being trapped in such eternal supper, sharing the table with the two siblings whose twisted smiles remain, to this day, a mystery to us all.

In her eyes, haughty by lineage, but troubled by a pain that struggled not to reveal itself, burned a compassion she did not expect to find. She leaned towards me gracefully and, extending her hand, spoke: "Oh, unexpected visitor... leave behind your troubles and worries. Put aside the hunger that grips you and the weariness that bends your bones. You are under my roof, and as long as I have breath, you will lack nothing. Here you can rest, recover your spirit after the hard journey, and hunger will be nothing but a distant memory”.

It attracted and confused me at the same time, as if it wished to lead me and lose me in the same gesture. And I, unable to resist, advanced after it, driven by an inevitable curiosity. When I reached the clearing, I saw a full moon rising over a lake of dark waters and unfathomable depths.

lore.en: Yes, my daughter. On nights like this, when the mist descends and settles amongst the trees, the Miracle opens its windows just enough to show us what we have never seen before. It brings remote places to our side as if they had always slept here, barely a step away from our hands. But the mist is cunning, my child. If we venture into it, it will lay its deceptive veil upon us. It will blur the brilliance of the full moon, distort the paths, and open roads that never existed. That is why I beg you, my daughter, not to go out on nights like this. Even if the forest shimmers under the mist as if it holds a beautiful secret, do not heed its call. There are lights that only shine to lead us astray.

My destiny is to spend my last days secluded in a solitude so profound that not even the echoes of these long corridors dare to accompany me. Oh, Miracle… I once feared you with the fervour of one who knows your implacable hand; but now, here is what remains of me. I no longer fear you, nor will I ever fear you again. If my castle is to become my tomb, so be it. May the stones that were once my pride ultimately be my eternal guardians...".

*On a stormy night, a woman with her face hidden under a veil knocked, soaked to the bone, at the castle gates. From the outside I could see the lights on, and the beautiful sound of chamber music escaped through the cracks, suggesting a long, perhaps endless, celebration.*
 
 *The woman decided to wait. She settled herself as best she could under the eaves, hoping the party would end and someone would finally come to let her in. But the music did not stop; neither did the laughter, nor the festive murmur that seemed to resist the passage of time. Exhausted, she fell asleep in front of the imposing wooden doors.*
 
 *When she awoke, everything was different. A heavy silence filled the air, the moon shone with unusual intensity, and the rain had subsided completely. As she sat up, she discovered that the castle gates were ajar. Cautiously, she peered inside. Then she saw everything.*

 *The corpses lay scattered across the long corridor, motionless, their faces contorted in expressions of suffering. The music, the light and the laughter that hours before had seemed endless had completely faded away. Terrified, the woman backed away. And without looking back, she fled that cursed place, her tears mingling with the veil still damp from the storm.*�

lore.en:
No one could ever forget that woman. Every night she went deep into the forest to await the mist. She remained kneeling in the open air, motionless, murmuring prayers over and over again, begging the Miracle to make the mist return.

No one ever knew why she made such a request. Some claimed that the mist had taken something, or someone, she loved deeply, and that she therefore awaited its return: so that, upon its return, the mist would claim her as well.

One night, however, the woman did not appear. Worried, we went into the forest to look for her. All we found was her long white headdress tangled in the roots of an old tree. Of her, there was no trace. Perhaps the mist returned, as she had asked, and took her away, never to return her.

Since then, every night when the mist thickens, we place her headscarf at the entrance to the forest. We do this so that she will protect us, or so that the mist, seeing it, will be satiated by her memory and continue on its way without taking anyone else.

That night the old painter was visited by the strangest and most disturbing of dreams. He saw himself as a guest at the table of two elders, siblings that engrossed themselves to the bitter vice of mutual disdain. Already sitting, they shot him uncomfortable smiles, and offered a meagre excuse for a dinner. The oldest, Castula, barraged her brother Trifon in constant slander, that he retorted back with disregard in an endless back and forth. Now and then they grinned at the painter, gestures loaded with hypocrisy that only made their cadaveric faces the more unsettling.

Shaken by the macabre surrounding that vision, the artist woke up in a flash of inspiration, and decided to capture that weird and anxious nightmare. The outlandish dream was then immortalised in a grim painting that invited the beholder to step inside the frame. Even if, by doing so, they risked being trapped in such eternal supper, sharing the table with the two siblings whose twisted smiles remain, to this day, a mystery to us all.

It was a night of unusual beauty, of clarity and quietness. Within the circle of high towers that had always been my home, only silence. I stayed in the great balcony, like every night, so I could offer a prayer to the starry sky. A rotund, full moon shined closer than ever, bathing everything in bluish and purple shades. I immersed myself in my litany, inspired by the holiness of such moment.

Suddenly, a shimmer in the sky caught my attention, and I was left breathless by the vision. A huge basilica, tall, sublime and of an impossibly transparent turquoise colour, stood askew before me, surrounded by the circle of towers. I knew then that everything was true. The great construction of watchtowers named the crown, had been built because of a legend. A legend of a ghost-like basilica that only in the light of the full moon revealed itself.

The same building had once stood there, before crumbling into the ground in ancient times. The devout witnesses dedicated their lives to watch that place, praying for another glimpse of that sacred sight, and so built the circle of towers that I now call home, around the point where that Miracle took place.

It was then when we made way for the leper that, wearing filthy rags, awaited in the threshold of our modest hospice. We kept our distance, terrified by the risk of infection, the sick man stumbling towards our master. He was, however, unfazed by his presence. With determination, and to everyone’s astonishment, our master kneeled before the leper. He then took his sleeve and revealed the purulent flesh of a shivering hand. 

“May the Miracle, through this osculum, shower you with its protection and its grace.” he said, before kissing the bare hand of that leper, who seeing this, could not hold back his tears.

That malnourished child walked under a scorching sun that made the earth boil under his wounded, bare feet. He walked with the aid of a dried, twisted root that served as a cane and poorly helped to lessen the burning pain that came with every step. He walked with his face down, averting his eyes from the blinding glare of that cruel light. Only looking up every now and then to squint his eyes and make sure that, far in the horizon, the Great City was still there. The one that’s name he didn’t know, that majestically towered like a mountain in the middle of the barren desert.

When the child, after such an exhausting ordeal, finally reached the city, he felt his hopes crumbling to dust. For there, he was greeted only by misery and desolation. By faces withered by pain and loss, starving bodies crawling down streets and grieving souls that wept in near silence. The city was but a haven for the lost, a ruined maze where only hellish suffering could be found. Filled by despair, the child’s eye searched the sky in sorrow. There, just above the city, hovered a vast cloud, thicker than any other, dyed in pinks and orange shades by the twilight sun that was about to hide behind the distant mountains. Enraptured by the beauty of such vision, he observed as that the shape seemingly moulded itself into a heart of colossal proportions.

lore.en:
Once Crisanta saw the blood flowing from her wounds, she realised she could never stop the Miracle from taking flesh. She had been fighting the Archconfraternity of Penitents in a long, cruel conflict, but defeat was now inevitable.

Eviterno lead the congregation, a peerless foe whose impossible power was fed by the endless sources of his divine eternity. The Miracle had chosen him to be the protector of its new work, after bestowed upon him the Original Penitence: that of perpetual contemplation. To wait endlessly, until the Miracle required so. And so was he called to arms, in the vigil of the new celestial icon birth, the great divine work that would join the hearts of the devout and bring together their faith.

Eviterno, father of Penitents, heeded the call and fought in that decisive battle, where Crisanta met defeat. Exhausted, Crisanta fell to the cold floor of that temple, knowing she was living through her last moments as that magnificent creation ripped through the bloodied skies above them all. That ancient sacred ground would be her tomb, but also where her fiery legacy would persist: her sword.

In that very moment she held her steel up, wrapped as it was in crimson and plunged it fearlessly into her chest. In her very blood she bathed it, a final sacrifice bestowed to its future wielder. Only then did Crisanta allow her eyelids to fall, concealed by the metallic severity of her helmet, and only then did those eyes, that had always remained vigilant within their own darkness, shut forever. Submerged in the night of her blind, unshakable, faith.

lore.en:
His Last Work. Part I

Dawn was yet to break, and the air was cold and still when the sculptor left his workshop, wandering in despair. His soul yearned for the sweet breath of inspiration. His hands ready for a new work. He paced down the labyrinthine streets of his hometown, the city where he had dedicated his life to an art that had always been his call: the carving of holy effigies, the sculpting of saints and martyrs.

description.en: Metal blade with a pronounced curve. With it, sculptors carve and sculpt the wood with extreme delicacy to produce precise contours in their work.

lore.en:
His Last Work. Part II

There was no corner of the city he didn’t know, no hidden passage, extravagant shortcut or dangerous alley foreign to his memory. He walked, agitated, in long and loud strides, his eyes darting around in search for a muse, for that which awoke his misplaced artistic desires.

After hours spent drifting without a purpose, a ruckus found his ears from a street nearby. Moved by curiosity, he followed the uproar, and what he saw froze the blood in his veins: two men duelled with knives, their bodies pierced with slashes that shined like shoals of scarlet fish. They fought as blood soaked their clothes, staring at each other with eyes full of spite and fear.

description.en: Phial of brightly coloured oil. By mixing its contents with different pigments, the sculptors obtained a wide variety of hues with which to colour their work.

lore.en:
His Last Work. Part III

The old sculptor took cover and crouched in fear, but could not avert his eyes from such a savage affray. Suddenly, a woman appeared in their midst, arms high, hoping to cease their bloody endeavour. Blind by hate, the fighters could do nothing to avoid a dreadful end: she fell to the ground, mortally wounded.[

lore.en: For years, the echoes of my agonising breath were the only sounds to reach my ears in this forsaken church of the afflicted. But suddenly, a thunder rocked the world outside these walls, a powerful beating that shook the ground, the columns and my tired old bones. And then I knew. That heartbeat was nothing but a call to a new mass. Its sound announced to each of us the return of our faith. The return of the Miracle. At such moment did hope return to our forlorn hearts.

description.en: Cloth whose paint streaks depict the shape of a face. Blessed Regula wore it as a veil as a symbol of veneration for the saint, to whom she dedicated her life and death.

lore.en:
One night, the young Regula, and we will never know if she did this out of curiosity or boredom, crept into the workshop of the famous sculptress of her village.

She wanted to be the first to behold her newest piece, the one so eagerly waited for by everyone: the effigy of the Saint. She froze, just as she entered, struck with awe in the presence of such beautiful work, which paint had still to dry. Regula then felt a perverse urge, and taking a cloth, pressed down against the face of the Saint, stealing all colour from the sculpture visage.

She then covered her own face with the fabric, pretending that the Saint’s beauty was now hers. The young woman played with her painted cloth, mimicking the pious gesture of the Saint, dreaming of the villagers' devotion.

After which, it was time to leave, lest the sculptress discovered her mischief. But upon removing the cloth she discovered, horrified, that the reflection on one of the windows showed no features of her face. In its place remained a shapeless stump of ashen flesh, dry and cracked like charred wood. Regula’s scream pierced the night, as she understood the punishment for her sin.

description.en: Manuscript belonging to the cantankerous old man who dwells in the Hamlet of the Golden Knots. It contains a list of names that cover the parchment in ink from beginning to end.

lore.en: The text was illegible, written in its entirety with a penmanship as nervous as it was erratic. Letters intertwined, overlapped and ran in chaotic courses. Some, so small they were barely noticeable. The paper was smudged, scratched, ran through with strokes askew. All of it gave the strong impression that the author had been rushed, be it by fear or anxiety. Or perhaps their intention had been different: to confuse, to erase their trace. To conceal.

That cloth brought Castula feelings of warmth and calm, but also awakened within her a deep curiosity. The present concealed something only she could barely perceive, something that whispered in a language of embroidery and soft folds. Perhaps she just imagined it all?

description.en: Symbol of an old man who never recognised the affection he felt for his sister.

lore.en:
That night the old painter was visited by the strangest and disturbing of dreams. He saw himself as a guest to the table of two elders, siblings that engrossed themselves to the bitter vice of mutual disdain. Already sitting, they shot him uncomfortable smiles, and offered a meagre excuse for a dinner. The oldest, Castula, barraged her brother Trifon in constant slander, that he retorted back with disregard in an endless back and forth. Now and then they grinned at the painter, gestures loaded with hypocrisy that only made their cadaveric faces the more unsettling.

Shaken by the macabre surrounding that vision, the artist woke up in a flash of inspiration, and decided to capture that weird and anxious nightmare. The outlandish dream was then immortalised in a grim painting that invited the beholder to step inside the frame. Even if, by doing so, they risked being trapped in such eternal supper, sharing the table with the two siblings whose twisted smiles remain, to this day, a mystery to us all.

As she removed them, her muddy palms began to gently spread the mud over the grave wounds of the dying man who lay before her, whose moans intertwined with the tremors of pain and the moans of terror. lore.en:
It is said that Edicta was born with her heart open like a wound. From childhood, sadness inhabited her like a silent guest, and she cried at every glimmer of pain she saw in the world, no matter how small. She found sorrow in weary faces, in animals that suffered in silence, even in leaves that the wind tore off prematurely. Her soul seemed to hear lament where others only perceived the inevitable course of life.

One morning, the entire town was awestruck, for from Edicta's tears sprang small, withered flowers, flowers that were born already defeated, as if their life were also a lament. This was taken as a sacred act of the Miracle. They said that Edicta wept for everyone, that her tears were relics worthy of being kept in small lachries to venerate the sorrow she carried for all the inhabitants of Cvstodia.

But what began as reverence turned to greed. People followed and harassed her, not only to collect her tears, but to pry them out. They told her of other people's misfortunes and fabricated tragedies, surrounded her with feigned lamentations, led her to places where death or sorrow had left their mark – all to force her to weep ever more tears. Her compassion, which had been a gift, became a punishment. And so, broken by the greed of others and with tears as her only guide, Edicta fled to the far reaches of Cvstodia.

After a long, aimless journey, Edicta found refuge in a cloistered convent, carved underground into frozen land hardened by perpetual snowstorms. There, in icy corridors that resembled tombs, she could weep without being pursued. The sisters watched her pass by, forever clutching her cameo, forever trembling, weeping for life and for death, for what was lost and for what still hurts. Edicta prayed every night, begging to be able to weep freely, without arousing desire or covetousness.

It was then that the Miracle heard her. One early morning, as the young woman sobbed in the icy gloom of her cell, a new face descended upon her like a sealed blessing. A carved face of polished, varnished wood, with a sweet and serene expression, that would forever conceal her weeping face. A face that could never be removed, for the Miracle had joined it to her flesh to protect her from the world and the world from her pain.

And from that day on, not a single tear escaped her visible eyes. It is said that, beneath her serene mask, Edicta continued to weep silently so that only the Miracle could witness the truth of her sorrow.

description.en: Heavy and eroded fragment of the golden mask of Asterion. Its face reveals an expression of ancient guilt, so dense that it seems to have permeated the metal.

lore.en:
The young Asterion appeared one day in the middle of an endless desert, reduced to skin and bones, with his memory in tatters. He knew neither his origin, nor what absurd path had led him to that scorching ocean of pale dunes. There he was found by some pilgrims, guided by a gigantic warrior dragging a colossal censer, so disproportionate that it seemed to defy all logic.

During the nights, while the camp slept, Asterion watched the warrior. He saw him bend down toward his strange censer covered with old, threadbare rags, as if secret voices emanated from that object, voices only he could decipher. The warrior nodded gravely, murmuring answers in a language the boy couldn't understand.

 The journey was cruel. Under the weight of the sun and the endless distance that offered no refuge, the pilgrims fell one after another, consumed by exhaustion. The warrior lifted them, carried them on his shoulders, trying to save them while the enormous censer continued its relentless drag across the sand. Despite everything, one by one they fell behind… until only the warrior and the young Asterion continued, whose frailty concealed a surprising resilience and will.

One day they entered a region of the desert where the wind roared like a rabid animal. The sand floated in the air, forming a dense, blinding fog. There, amidst the gusts, Asterion saw the rags wrapped around the censer tear off and fly away. Then he understood, horrified, that it was not a mere ritual object, and that beneath the rags lay an urn of crystal and gold, and inside it rested a mummified body, curled up like an ascetic who had waited centuries for the moment of awakening.

Before he could ask anything, a colossal, amorphous creature emerged from the storm. The warrior turned to Asterion and said in a grave voice, "This is where your apprenticeship will begin, brother”.

The beast charged violently. Asterion could barely make out shapes through the windswept sand that stung his eyes. But he saw the warrior bring his ear close to the incense burner and begin that reverential whisper again. And then a ferocious, almost animalistic energy seemed to ignite within him. The warrior launched himself into battle with tremendous strength.

The fight was long and brutal. Warrior and creature were evenly matched, two exhausted titans refusing to fall. It was then that Asterion, wiping the sand from his face, decided to act. Unarmed and unprotected, he lunged at the creature. His small size allowed him to instinctively dodge the monstrous swipes, and his desperate attack distracted the beast just enough.

 The warrior seized that moment. With a shout that echoed like thunder in the midst of a storm, he delivered the final blow. The creature collapsed, lifeless, sinking into the sand from which it had spawned.

 The sandy mist began to dissipate. The silence of the desert returned, vast and absolute.

The warrior approached Asterion, placed a heavy hand on his shoulder, and said:

 "He who rests within my weapon was my master. When your training is complete, you will wield a similar weapon... and I will sleep within it. Thus I will be able to guide you from the other side of sleep. Thus I will remain with you, always”.

lore.en:
"Dear anonymous reader,

If thou readest these lines, it is because thine curiosity has suppressed thine will. Thou hast dared to open this sealed letter, thus committing a grave crime and illegitimately taking possession of that which it contains, which is none other than my curse. Thine is, now, as thine had been the sin.

With these words, inscribed in black ink, I curse thee to follow in my footsteps, the same footsteps of another sinner I followed, and another, and another, and another, thus perpetuating the curse.

The first step of the one who seeks redemption lies in performing an act of humility. For this, thou must seek out the largest looking glass, prostrate thyself before thine reflection, look thyself in the eye and beg forgiveness."

lore.en:
And then the Miracle witnessed a drama unfolding in three acts. Three sins woven from pain, guilt and lies.

The First Sin: Pride.

In the most remote lands of Cvstodia, rising from the icy mist, stood a vast castle, a refuge for nobles who, oblivious to the torment afflicting the rest of Cvstodia, lived surrounded by worldly luxuries and secular customs. Their castle, more a sanctuary of excess than virtue, remained aloof from the suffering that the Miracle inflicted upon the rest of humanity.

But that irreverent prosperity did not go unnoticed. The Miracle, in its inscrutable severity, gave rise to a devastating curse within the castle. An invisible force consolidated its hold on the castle, transforming it into an inhabited tomb. From the weary chests of its inhabitants emerged a dark mist, dense as a malevolent omen. And from that unholy exhalation sprouted enormous nails that, guided by a cruel and inexorable will, sought the flesh that had summoned them. One after another they sank into chests and sides, piercing their victims amidst stifled screams, until every hall, corridor and chamber was filled with shivering bodies and eyes still wide with terror.

One by one all its inhabitants perished, until only Duchess Crescencia remained alive, sick and trapped in her stone prison.

Even in her illness, the Duchess survived, condemned to a solitude as profound as the disease that consumed her. In her despair, she raised prayers to the Miracle, begging not to die alone, that her last breath not be lost in the void.

description.en: Carved blackened silver ring bearing the upper half of a lady's face. The figure's sealed eyelids suggest a deep sleep.

lore.en:
The Second Sin: Perfidy.

The Miracle listened. One day, a wandering man, exhausted and hungry, named Eliseo, arrived at the castle. He was pious, of noble blood, but he had renounced his privileges to travel Cvstodia, contemplate the designs of the Miracle and offer help to those in need.

The Duchess welcomed him within the walls of her isolation, and soon a silent love germinated in her heart, ultimately destined to misfortune. Unable to contain it, she ended up revealing it. The man, moved more by pity than desire, responded with a white lie: he said he reciprocated her affection to ease the noblewoman's soul, torn apart by loneliness. Then, overcome by her own frailty, she confessed the illness that was consuming her final days and begged him not to let her die alone. She beseeched him to, when the time came, prepare her body for burial and watch over her eternal rest.

The man accepted, moved by compassion and affection. He kept his promise. He prepared the Duchess's body and settled down to watch over her. But when he tried to rise from the coffin, he discovered that strange nails were pinning his hands, preventing him from escaping.

That colossal door seemed to resist, as if some dark will were clinging to it from the other side. Even so, I managed to open it with some effort. An icy wind suddenly burst in, scratching my skin and my aching eyes. Before me lay a clear night, bathed in the round light of the full moon. It invited me to cross over, to lose myself in its clarity. But something invisible held me back.

Dead stares. Part III of III

An indescribable force gripped my legs and, with them, my own will. I felt something icy and sharp pierce my back, paralysing me. I couldn't turn around to see what it was, where such a terrible, stabbing pain was coming from. I felt my strength dissipate, my body succumbing to the weight of exhaustion. The night beyond the threshold began to fade before my eyes; the room darkened, slowly swallowing every reflection. Suddenly, the corpses surrounding me finally closed their dead eyes.
Mine, obediently, closed as well.

lore.en:
Only the Penitent of Virtue knows, deep in his heart, whether the path he has taken is the right one, and whether each step taken has led him to ultimate forgiveness. Only he knows the true relief that comes after shedding the weight of guilt, and the peace that is born when remorse stops burning and becomes an offering.

The armour of the Penitent of Virtue will protect him from irreparable harm, but it will not save him from the pain of the flesh. And the masked helm that conceals his face will preserve his anonymity, for only in intimate communion with the Miracle can the promised absolution be attained.

Here lie the ashes of that Penitent of Virtue who, consumed in his final sacrifice, breathed his last with the certainty of having been forgiven.

lore.en:
The Second Sin: Perfidy.

The Miracle listened. One day, a wandering man, exhausted and hungry, named Eliseo, arrived at the castle. He was pious, of noble blood, but he had renounced his privileges to travel Cvstodia, contemplate the designs of the Miracle and offer help to those in need.

The Duchess welcomed him within the walls of her isolation, and soon a silent love germinated in her heart, ultimately destined to misfortune. Unable to contain it, she ended up revealing it. The man, moved more by pity than desire, responded with a white lie: he said he reciprocated her affection to ease the noblewoman's soul, torn apart by loneliness. Then, overcome by her own frailty, she confessed the illness that was consuming her final days and begged him not to let her die alone. She beseeched him to, when the time came, prepare her body for burial and watch over her eternal rest.

The man accepted, moved by compassion and affection. He kept his promise. He prepared the Duchess's body and settled down to watch over her. But when he tried to rise from the coffin, he discovered that strange nails were pinning his hands, preventing him from escaping.

The Third Sin: Abjuration.

The curse had answered the Duchess's plea, and as long as he remained nailed to the coffin, her spirit would not depart for the afterlife but would remain trapped in the castle along with her love for that man.

Thus, Duchess Crescencia had dared to defy even the Miracle, ignoring the will that had been imposed upon her. She refused to breathe her last, refused to cross the threshold of eternal sleep, clinging desperately to a love that was never more than a reflection, a whisper invented to soothe her loneliness.

In her obstinacy, she deceived the man, herself and the Miracle, perpetuating a lie so profound that it kept her spirit in the castle, chained to a desire that never had flesh or truth.

lore.en:
How will they know the truth, if to their eyes I'm no different from the others? We all share the same beauty and grandeur, the same skin made from light itself, the same voice that sounds like a gift from the heavens. What if I was, in fact, different? What if I truly was the most divine of them all, the only one deserving adoration?

Yes… all will kneel before me, all will worship me, all will wait eternities to share my presence and fight for the honour of kissing my flesh…

I just need to ensure the others disappear.

description.en: A coin that was used for many years as payment for the processions that traversed the roads at night-time. These processions gradually died out, so finding a coin like this is a rare occurrence.

lore.en:
The thick night mists snaked and curled around the lattice of trunks and branches that made out that forest. From that very fog, that sticked to my skin like a clammy shroud, did emerge the shadows. They marched in procession with mournful parsimony, each one a bearer of their own lament and grim expression, confused, wafting forward in death. Seized by this sinister sight, I could not help but witness, frozen in place, as they slowly made their way towards me.

Only then did the procession stop. The shadow guiding the group (the tallest and most tenebrous of them all) bowed down, in silence, showing me the palm of his bare hand. He was waiting for something. Petrified, I could but mutter a few vain words whilst my whole being shivered; it was at that moment that the piercing light of a sudden dawn broke through the entangled canopy of that forest, tearing apart both fog and spectre, making them all vanish before me. The sweet song of birds conjured away the deadly silence that had reigned before. I will never know what tribute that ghost of mists would have asketh for, nor if I will ever encounter them again.

description.en: Cord knot whose origins have long been forgotten. Skilled hands could join this knot to the strings that hold the rosary beads.

lore.en: Knot after knot, bead after bead, with the most composed of patience, I thread the rosary. Each bead a guilt, a mourning, a confession, a step in the long ladder of penance. And through the threshold of this grim haven, forgotten by all, will enter those that seek my assistance, those that seek this old and sacred craft of mine, those that will face the light shed by the candles of my roof, whoever they are. And they shall then bask on the shelter and the hope they provide. I will, until that moment, wait, knot after knot, bead after bead, with the most composed of patience.

lore.en: And now I know of my punishment, and I know its name is Death. Not my own, but that of others, that of everything around me. I witness death as it erases all that surrounds my being, all happiness, beauty and hope harboured in the hearts of those I once called close. Doomed to solitude, to the blackness found behind these cold bars, behind this heavy curtain that only my voice can pierce. Moribund as they sound, my words are all that I can use to warn the fools that try to approach this place. No one knows my name, nor my pain. And so, I can only wait, wait that someday might the Miracle take mercy on me, and free me from this curse.

lore.en:
The church shut its doors to us, forever. The floor of its nave collapsed, revealing a deep, dark abyss. A remnant of a bygone era, that had been concealed for centuries. Only those brave enough dare to peer into its blackness and they speak of walls carved with figures, looking upwards in unison, as if yearning for the scarce light. 

They also say that sometimes, those who stayed for a while, could hear a distant wail. A cry so desperate it wounded the soul, and no one knew from where or from what horror it came. A sound that could never be forgotten. 

When that happens, they throw white flowers into the abyss, an act that apparently calms down the suffering of that mysterious being. No one knows whether the flowers are thrown as a gesture of compassion or fear. No one knows what lies there, in the depths of the abyss, only that we must stay away from that place.

lore.en:
On hearing the young man's question, the elder’s gaze filled with melancholy: “Yes, this church belongeth to a bygone age, one so ancient, so chaotic, that it's as if it wanted to disappear from memory. An age in which time itself decided to stop in a perpetual sunset, and in which every man yearned only for the designs of the divine. But so it happened that the faith of those people faded, quietly escaping from their hearts year after year. Even so, this abandoned church still stands, its foundations as firm as ever, as if it waited for something. As if it refused to give up the faith that so many had already lost…”

And the old man stood there, gazing at the sturdy stone, lost in thought.

The voice spoke of a penance that would grow my body into a great statue. That would empty my insides leaving only the bones, enveloped in scarlet velvet. That would unfold my skin, as if it was a blessed mantle, revealing the hollow skeleton below.

description.en: An oversized toy from a purer, happier time. The guardian of the High Gardens will rejoice in its return.

lore.en: When faith withers from people’s hearts, that is when the Holy Brothers of the Golden Visage drift away. They vanish in the wind, fading like a dream in the morning light. As from hope they are born, and without it they wane. Proximo, as the eldest of them, watched over the children, but the designs of the Miracle anchored him to the ground, condemning him to follow their departure with nothing but a longing gaze. He then raises the old rattle, his only memento left from his divine origin, and softly shakes it. A sweet tinkling resonates in the air and travels with the wind, a quiet beckoning. So the Holy Brothers know that they are never alone, that someone is waiting for them. And they feel a pang inside them, a longing call, wherever they are. Wherever the wind had taken them.

description.en: Symbol of the guardian of the High Gardens, admired by all his brothers.C

lore.en: Proximo felt his strength falter, he felt himself descend from the clouds like a dry leaf carried by a sudden gale. As he fell, confused and too weak to fly, he saw the light around him turn red and dark, as an abundance of clouds shadowed the sky with a sanguine, garnet colour. The Miracle had returned.

description.en: One of the seeds for those who dwell in secrecy. The Sleepless Ones will arise for the one in need of genuine protection.

lore.en: The massive tower that loomed so imposingly before us, had no known origin. It seemed like it had always existed, a sentinel for the centuries, watching with unmoving sternness. Its architecture was foreign to us, weird, as if its top had been severed by an impossible blade. Incomplete as it was, its many windows oozed with a waxy, opaque substance, that sealed every access to the monument. The tower's warning to those who would see its ancestral silence broken.

description.en: Gift of the Anonymous Pilgrim. It opens the first of the cages in the Chapel of the Five Doves.

lore.en: It happened right there, in that sacred chapel. The Miracle itself melted glass into an urn and dressed it with gold, so it could properly display the inert body of that pious young man. The one that was chosen by the divine to witness every event brought by the return of the Faith. The one that gave his life, and who was preserved incorruptible so his testimony will remain immortal. The testimony of the New Birth of the Miracle.

description.en: Key plundered from the remains of Benedicta, the ghost of the Basilica. It opens the second of the cages in the Chapel of the Five Doves.

lore.en:
Under the light of the candles did the cardinals corpses lay, within sinister crystal caskets. They were the chosen by the Endless Orison, a congregation of sisters that devoted themselves to honour the deceased, with their perpetual prayer. Each time a new body arrived, one of them volunteered as their warden, and so dedicate her daily prayers to their soul until the end of her days. Then another sister would take her place, and so the rite would continue.

One night, the coffin of a new cardinal arrived the basilica, and the sisters surrounded it to prepare their ritual. At that moment, the sister Benedicta stepped forward, carrying a frayed scroll, and everyone immediately knew the parchment for what it was... the apocryphal prayer. Those ancient verses carried a terrible power. Whoever uttered its inked words would be imprisoned in eternal prayer, unable to stop until they died of starvation. Sister Benedicta kneeled and started her chant, as the others fled the room in fear, closing the door upon leaving. They knew Benedicta had sealed her fate, but not the reasons behind that act of sacrifice. Even though centuries have already passed, some sisters swear, that the white spectre of Benedicta can still be seen during the darkest nights, praying at the cardinal's sepulchre.

description.en: Key plundered from the remains of Odón, the Cathedral's protector. It opens the third of the cages in the Chapel of the Five Doves.�

lore.en:
As if awakened from the most terrible dream, the warriors’ eyes opened together. Dazed still, they tried to recall the moments before. Their ship capsized, they had hopelessly drowned in the icy depths of the ocean, merciless reaper of lives. But now there was a ceiling over their heads. A ceiling of a rapturous beauty, ornated with the most delicate engravings.

They looked at each other, at the salt that crusted their bodies, and at the seaweed and coral that protruded from their armour. With parched throats, cracked lips and wretched faces they looked at Odon, their burly captain, as he slowly rose. The salt in his armour crunched as he moved, as he thrust his halberd into the clammy stone floor. He looked silently at them in turn, gaze hidden behind his impervious mask. He knew where they were. This had to be the cathedral the Miracle had long hidden under the dark waters of the sea. Salt had granted them life, and he knew his new orders were clear. To guard this sacred place, and to do so until their deaths. Death they would not fear, for they had already conquered it once.

description.en: Key plundered from the remains of Sínodo, the Curse of the Severed Tower. It opens the fourth of the cages in the Chapel of the Five Doves.�

lore.en:
The old pontiff walked down the vast hallways of the holy palace, under the gaze of huge paintings that depicted every pontiff that had come before him in the ancient land of Cvstodia. Their stern, solemn faces followed him, as if they recognized him as the last of their line. He stopped before one of them and announced:

“All of our venerable and pontifical visages will one day escape from these paintings, leaving them hollow and devoid of sanctity. And they will all together sprout again from the folds of a colossal and golden cappa magna, alive and full of ornament and blessings. And our voices will sing in perfect unison, and the hymns they will sing will stand eternal. For the Miracle wills it so.”

description.en: Key plundered from the remains of Svsona, Tormented in Two Moons. It opens the last of the cages in the Chapel of the Five Doves.

lore.en:
The lake was a mirror. The palace could be seen in its reflection, a memory of what once existed. Only the Miracle allowed us such sight, as the palace was long lost. They say the old bell, the one in the highest tower, plummeted down and sank in the lake, where no one could ever retrieve it from.

But one night, with the moon at its fullest, something strange happened. Within the surface of the lake, the bell could be seen, hanging on top of its tower, like it had never fallen. And then it tolled. A deep, sombre toll that reverberated and tore the silence apart. The lake rippled, and its waters wrinkled like the skin of an old man. The waves spread along the surface, crossing each other, tracing creases and folds that distorted the reflection of the palace.

Those watching the lake witnessed in horror how their own reflections changed shape. Their faces stretched and twisted, their eyes sank within their skulls, their mouths opened agape in impossible, silent screams. That was the curse of the bell. What they saw in the water was not a distorted reflection now, but reality: abominable creatures, damned for eternity.

description.en: Phial of consecrated oil. The priests commissioned perfumers to make oils to anoint the weapons of soldiers in battle, so as to bless their souls and increase their morale.�

lore.en:
"The priest slowly lifted the thick slate that covered the coffin, still covered by the moisture of earth, and the dust inside swirled in the air. He introduced a trembling hand under the luxurious liturgic garments that dressed the corpse of the pontiff. Looking for something that only he knew was there. A tiny ornated phial whose knot, braided in different colours, effortlessly unravelled in his hands. Dense and dark oils stirred inside the depths of the phial.

The priest felt a chill and could not help looking at the withered and grey skull of the pontiff. It seemed to regard him from beneath his empty, blackened sockets. He clenched the flask in his fingers and quickly fled from that place, feeling the cold pontiff's stare, as a dagger on his back.""

description.en: The charred remains of the figures of the Four Envoys, salvaged from the embers. The ashes shall mark as worthy the skin of the one who performs the Ultimate Sacrifice thus returning to the heavens.

lore.en: …And we four shall descend, waving our immaculate canvases in the fine wind, and our blessing will then be thine. The Great Grace will then bestow upon thee the ultimate forgiveness. For our mere presence means absolution, and that is but the last step to walk in the Way of Penitence.

description.en: The tip of an object of worship that was turned into a weapon. It delivered a violent end to countless enemies, and the memories of those deaths linger on. Its strength resides in the Arsenal of Penitence, in which it can be awakened.

lore.en:
The night was dark and full of mist. Yerma saw her chance to climb in through an open window, breaking into that old church that discreetly oversaw a far corner of the village. A perfect night for her purpose. 

With cat-like agility she climbed down a sculpture on the inner facade, until reaching the cold marble floor. Nobody saw or heard her. She stepped into the temple's blackness, her eyes piercing every shadow in search of her objective. And there it was, on top of an altar at the end of the nave. A silver rod, an old sacred relic that had remained intact despite the centuries. It shone with a glow of its own, like some kind of living thing.

It was said that the rod had been plated with an impossible alloy of oil-anointed silver. Yerma didn’t hesitate. She slid from the shadows like a snake, took the rod and felt its cold weight. That argent glow fleetingly reflected in her eyes, revealing them to be full of hate and thirsty for vengeance. Nobody will ever know what happened to that holy artifact.

description.en: Symbol of the wrapped agony, who made the ultimate sacrifice to prevent the catastrophe.]

lore.en:
Once Crisanta saw the blood flowing from her gashing wound she realized she could never stop the Miracle from taking flesh. She had been fighting the Archconfraternity of Penitents in a long, cruel conflict, but defeat was now inevitable. Eviterno led the congregation, a peerless foe whose impossible power was fed by the endless sources of his divine eternity. The Miracle had chosen him protector of its new work, after bestowing upon him the Original Penitence: that of perpetual contemplation.  To wait endlessly, until the Miracle required so. And so was he called to arms, in the vigil of the new celestial icon birth, the great divine work that would join the hearts of the devout and bring together their faith. And Eviterno, father of Penitents, heeded the call and fought in that decisive battle, where Crisanta met defeat. 

Exhausted, Crisanta fell to the cold slates of that temple, knowing she was living through what she knew would be her last moments, and resignated as that magnificient creation ripped through the bloodied skies, above them all. That ancient sacred ground would be her tomb, but also where her fiery legacy would persist: her sword. In that very moment she held her steel up, wrapped as it was in crimson, and plunged it fearlessly into her chest. In her very blood she bathed it, a final sacrifice that she bestowed to its future wielder. 

Only then did Crisanta allow her eyelids to fall, concealed by the metallic severity of her helmet, and only then did those eyes, that had always remained vigilant within their own darkness, shut forever. Submerged in the night of her blind, unshakable, faith.
